findings.summary: Fish completion script breaks because the three-line completion output is already split per line by `set -l response (...)`, so `string split \n` yields wrong items and `$metadata[2]`/`$metadata[3]` are empty, failing completion for every command.
The string `_` is used as a sentinel for 'no help', so an option whose real help text is `_` loses its description.
Newlines in help text are replaced with a literal `\n`, so Fish displays a visible backslash-n rather than a line break.
New tests only check the Python output format and never execute the Fish script, so they pass despite the script being unable to parse the new format.
